artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Enz Of An Era, released in 1982 on the Mushroom label, is a compilation album by Split Enz that encapsulates the band's evolution from their early art-rock beginnings to their more polished pop-rock sound. The album features a curated selection of tracks spanning their career up to that point, highlighting their distinctive blend of rock and pop with experimental and theatrical elements. This compilation serves as a retrospective that showcases the band's musical diversity and creative growth throughout the 1970s and early 1980s.

Positioned in Split Enz's discography after their string of successful studio albums, Enz Of An Era functions as a milestone summarizing their impact on the New Zealand and Australian music scenes. By 1982, Split Enz had established themselves as pioneers, being one of the first New Zealand acts to achieve international recognition. The album was released following a period of commercial success marked by chart-topping albums like Waiata (1981) and Time and Tide (1982), reflecting the band's transition from an avant-garde art-rock group to mainstream pop-rock artists.

Critically and commercially, Enz Of An Era was well received as it consolidated the band's legacy and introduced new listeners to their influential catalog. It highlighted their role in putting New Zealand music on the international stage and celebrated their creative achievements under the Mushroom label. The compilation remains a significant entry for fans and collectors, representing the breadth of Split Enz's innovative and genre-blending work up to the early 1980s.
